Claude Code agents should also read\\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\\n\\n## Project Overview\\n\\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\\naround $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of\\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\\\*=RE*\\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\\n\\nCI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and\\nmerges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through\\n`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before\\ndoing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the\\nrules.\\n\\nKey locations:\\n\\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\\\*=RE\\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\\\*\\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\\n  (`\\\\lean{}`, `\\\\leanok`)\\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer\\n\\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\\n\\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\\n\\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\\n\\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The\\npaper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and\\nproof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a\\nsorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is\\nalmost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\\n\\n## Repository Layout\\n\\n```\\nMIPStarRE/\\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\\n    ├── Preliminaries/\\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\\n    ├── Commutativity/\\n    └── Pasting/\\n```\\n\\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\\n\\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\\n\\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\\n\\n### First-time setup\\n\\n```bash\\nlake exe cache get\\nlake build\\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\\n```\\n\\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\\n\\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\\n\\n```bash\\nlake build\\n```\\n\\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\\n\\n```bash\\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\\n```\\n\\n### Check for proof holes in one file\\n\\n```bash\\nrg -n \\\"sorry|axiom\\\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\\n```\\n\\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\\n\\n```bash\\nrg -n \\\"sorry|axiom\\\" MIPStarRE\\n```\\n\\n### Declaration checker\\n\\n```bash\\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\\n```\\n\\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\\n\\n### Blueprint build\\n\\n```bash\\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\\n```\\n\\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\\n\\n### What counts as a single test\\n\\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\\nsingle-test commands are:\\n\\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\\n  `rg -n \\\"sorry|axiom\\\" path/to/File.lean || true`\\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\\n\\n### Recommended validation sequence\\n\\nFor a Lean file change:\\n\\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\\n\\nFor blueprint changes:\\n\\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\\n\\n## Toolchain\\n\\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\\n\\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\\n\\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\\n\\n## Proof-Filling Order\\n\\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\\n\\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\\n6. Section 12: pasting\\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\\n\\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\\n\\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\\n\\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\\nthe paper theorem.\\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\\n\\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\\\leanok` only\\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\\n\\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\\n\\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\\nfrom the blueprint by `\\\\lean{...}` and `\\\\leanok`.\\n\\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\\n`prop:*`):\\n\\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\\n   with `\\\\leanok`.\\n\\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\\n\\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\\n\\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\\n`\\\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\\n\\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\\nintegrity audit:\\n\\n- paper assumptions;\\n- Lean assumptions;\\n- paper conclusion;\\n- Lean conclusion;\\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\n\\n### Paper-realignment mode\\n\\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\\n\\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\\n\\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\\n\\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\\n\\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\\n\\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\\nhypotheses.\\n\\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\\nminimal form is:\\n\\n```text\\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\\n```\\n\\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\\ndeviation has been discharged.\\n\\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\\npaper hypotheses.\\n\\n## Code Conventions\\n\\n### Imports\\n\\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\\n- One import per line\\n- Follow existing local import style\\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\\n\\n### File structure\\n\\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\\n\\n1. imports\\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\\n3. namespace / opens / variables\\n4. declarations\\n\\n### Formatting\\n\\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\\n  own line\\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\\n  theorem statement\\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\\n  tactic blocks.\\n\\n### Naming conventions\\n\\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\\n\\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\\n\\nProject-preferred variable names:\\n\\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\\n- `σ` — strategies\\n- `P` — projective measurements\\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\\n\\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\\n\\n### Types and signatures\\n\\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\\n  wrappers\\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\\n\\n### Documentation\\n\\nRequired:\\n\\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\\n\\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\\\lean{...}`\\nand `\\\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\\n\\n## Proof Engineering\\n\\n### Search before proving\\n\\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\\n\\n### Mathlib integration\\n\\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\\n\\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\\n\\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\\n\\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\\n\\n### Validation ladder\\n\\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\\n2. `lake build`\\n\\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\\n\\n### Lean-specific advice\\n\\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\\n  already in the repo\\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\\n\\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\\n\\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\\nmathematical phrase is available.\\n\\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\\n\\n### Paper-gap notes\\n\\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\\n\\n## Proof Integrity\\n\\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\\n\\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\\n\\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\\n\\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\\n\\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\\n\\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\\n\\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\\n\\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\\nof this?*\\n\\n### Warnings\\n\\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\\nthe full warning catalog.\\n\\n### Anti-patterns\\n\\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\\n\\n## PR and Commit Conventions\\n\\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\\nparent project.\\n\\n### PR title format\\n\\n```\\ntype(scope): short description\\n```\\n\\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\\n\\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\\n\\n### PR body template\\n\\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\\n\\n```markdown\\n### Motivation\\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\\n\\n### Description\\n- State precisely what changed.\\n\\n### Testing\\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \\\"sorry|axiom\\\"`).\\n\\n---\\nAddresses #N\\n```\\n\\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\\n\\n### Commit messages\\n\\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\\\"Add\\\", not \\\"Added\\\")\\n- Subject under 72 characters\\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\\n\\n## Review Process\\n\\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\\n\\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\\\lean{}` and `\\\\leanok` tags for\\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\\n   a paper theorem.\\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\\n\\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\\n\\n## Blueprint Claude Code agents should also read\\\\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\\\\n\\\\n## Project Overview\\\\n\\\\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\\\\naround $MIP^* = RE$. Root imports\\\\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\\\\n\\\\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\\\\n\\\\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\\\\n\\\\n### First-time setup\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\nlake exe cache get\\\\nlake build\\\\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\\\\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\\\\n\\\\n## Toolchain\\\\n\\\\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\\\\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\\\\n\\\\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\\\\n\\\\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\\\\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\\\\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\\\\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\\\\n\\\\n## Proof-Filling Order\\\\n\\\\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\\\\n\\\\n1. Section 6: main induction wrapper\\\\n\\\\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\\\\n\\\\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\\\\n\\\\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\\\\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\\\\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\\\\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\\\\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\\\\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\\\\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\\\\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\\\\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\\\\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\\\\nthe paper theorem.\\\\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\\\\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\\\\n\\\\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\\\\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\\\\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\\\\\\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\\\\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\\\\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\\\\\\\leanok` only\\\\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\\\\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\\\\n\\\\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\\\\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\\\\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\\\\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\\\\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\\\\n\\\\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\\\\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\\\\nfrom the blueprint by `\\\\\\\\lean{...}` and `\\\\\\\\leanok`.\\\\n\\\\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\\\\n`prop:*`):\\\\n\\\\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\\\\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\\\\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\\\\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\\\\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\\\\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\\\\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\\\\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\\\\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\\\\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\\\\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\\\\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\\\\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\\\\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\\\\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\\\\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\\\\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\\\\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\\\\n   with `\\\\\\\\leanok`.\\\\n\\\\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\\\\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\\\\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\\\\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\\\\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\\\\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\\\\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\\\\n\\\\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\\\\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\\\\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\\\\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\\\\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\\\\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\\\\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\\\\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\\\\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\\\\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\\\\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\\\\n\\\\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\\\\n`\\\\\\\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\\\\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\\\\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\\\\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\\\\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\\\\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\\\\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\\\\n\\\\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\\\\nintegrity audit:\\\\n\\\\n- paper assumptions;\\\\n- Lean assumptions;\\\\n- paper conclusion;\\\\n- Lean conclusion;\\\\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\\\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\\\n\\\\n### Paper-realignment mode\\\\n\\\\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\\\\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\\\\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\\\\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\\\\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\\\\n\\\\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\\\\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\\\\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\\\\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\\\\n\\\\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\\\\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\\\\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\\\\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\\\\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\\\\n\\\\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\\\\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\\\\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\\\\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\\\\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\\\\n\\\\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\\\\n\\\\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\\\\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\\\\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\\\\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\\\\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\\\\nhypotheses.\\\\n\\\\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\\\\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\\\\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\\\\nminimal form is:\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\\\\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\\\\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\\\\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\\\\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\\\\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\\\\ndeviation has been discharged.\\\\n\\\\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\\\\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\\\\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\\\\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\\\\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\\\\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\\\\npaper hypotheses.\\\\n\\\\n## Code Conventions\\\\n\\\\n### Imports\\\\n\\\\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\\\\n- One import per line\\\\n- Follow existing local import style\\\\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\\\\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\\\\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\\\\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\\\\n\\\\n### File structure\\\\n\\\\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\\\\n\\\\n1. imports\\\\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\\\\n3. namespace / opens / variables\\\\n4. declarations\\\\n\\\\n### Formatting\\\\n\\\\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\\\\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\\\\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\\\\n  own line\\\\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\\\\n  theorem statement\\\\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\\\\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\\\\n  tactic blocks.\\\\n\\\\n### Naming conventions\\\\n\\\\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\\\\n\\\\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\\\\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\\\\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\\\\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\\\\n\\\\nProject-preferred variable names:\\\\n\\\\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\\\\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\\\\n- `σ` — strategies\\\\n- `P` — projective measurements\\\\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\\\\n\\\\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\\\\n\\\\n### Types and signatures\\\\n\\\\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\\\\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\\\\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\\\\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\\\\n  wrappers\\\\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\\\\n\\\\n### Documentation\\\\n\\\\nRequired:\\\\n\\\\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\\\\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\\\\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\\\\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\\\\n\\\\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\\\\\\\lean{...}`\\\\nand `\\\\\\\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\\\\n\\\\n## Proof Engineering\\\\n\\\\n### Search before proving\\\\n\\\\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\\\\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\\\\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\\\\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\\\\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\\\\n\\\\n### Mathlib integration\\\\n\\\\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\\\\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\\\\n\\\\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\\\\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\\\\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\\\\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\\\\n\\\\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\\\\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\\\\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\\\\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\\\\n\\\\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\\\\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\\\\n\\\\n### Validation ladder\\\\n\\\\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\\\\n2. `lake build`\\\\n\\\\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\\\\n\\\\n### Lean-specific advice\\\\n\\\\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\\\\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\\\\n  already in the repo\\\\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\\\\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\\\\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\\\\n\\\\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\\\\n\\\\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\\\\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\\\\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\\\\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\\\\nmathematical phrase is available.\\\\n\\\\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\\\\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\\\\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\\\\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\\\\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\\\\n\\\\n### Paper-gap notes\\\\n\\\\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\\\\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\\\\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\\\\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\\\\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\\\\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\\\\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\\\\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\\\\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\\\\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\\\\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\\\\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\\\\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\\\\n\\\\n## Proof Integrity\\\\n\\\\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\\\\n\\\\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\\\\n\\\\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\\\\n\\\\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\\\\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\\\\n\\\\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\\\\n\\\\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\\\\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\\\\n\\\\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\\\\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\\\\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\\\\n\\\\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\\\\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\\\\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\\\\nof this?*\\\\n\\\\n### Warnings\\\\n\\\\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\\\\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\\\\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\\\\nthe full warning catalog.\\\\n\\\\n### Anti-patterns\\\\n\\\\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\\\\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\\\\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\\\\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\\\\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\\\\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\\\\n\\\\n## PR and Commit Conventions\\\\n\\\\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\\\\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\\\\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\\\\nparent project.\\\\n\\\\n### PR title format\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\ntype(scope): short description\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\\\\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\\\\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\\\\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\\\\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\\\\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\\\\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\\\\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\\\\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\\\\n\\\\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\\\\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\\\\n\\\\n### PR body template\\\\n\\\\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n### Motivation\\\\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\\\\n\\\\n### Description\\\\n- State precisely what changed.\\\\n\\\\n### Testing\\\\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \\\\\\\"sorry|axiom\\\\\\\"`).\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\nAddresses #N\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\\\\n\\\\n### Commit messages\\\\n\\\\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\\\\\\\"Add\\\\\\\", not \\\\\\\"Added\\\\\\\")\\\\n- Subject under 72 characters\\\\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\\\\n\\\\n## Review Process\\\\n\\\\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\\\\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\\\\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\\\\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\\\\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\\\\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\\\\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\\\\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\\\\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\\\\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\\\\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\\\\n8. **Documentation** — Every new Concurrency, serialisation, recursion\\\\n\\\\n**Order.**  Within one invocation the phases run strictly\\\\n`ci → blueprint → review`, sequentially, in one process.  On GitHub this was a\\\\n`needs:` chain with the `!cancelled() && needs.setup.result == 'success'`\\\\nidiom, explained twice in the file because it was not obvious:\\\\n\\\\\\\"Serialized after CI fix to avoid parallel pushes to the same branch\\\\\\\"\\\\n(`auto-fix.yml:253-256`, `:282-285`).  Sequential function calls satisfy the\\\\nsame requirement trivially.  A phase that fails stops the ones after it; the\\\\nbranch is not handed to a second fixer in an unknown state.\\\\n\\\\n**Lock.**  A per-branch lock directory under\\\\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/fix-<branch>.lock` holds the running fix.  A\\\\nsecond invocation for the same branch writes a `cancel` sentinel into that\\\\ndirectory and waits: the holder checks the sentinel at every phase boundary and\\\\nexits cleanly if it is there.  That is `cancel-in-progress: true`\\\\n(`auto-fix.yml:259-261`) reproduced without a scheduler, and cleanly — a fix is\\\\nnever killed mid-edit, only stopped between phases.\\\\n\\\\nThe key is the **branch**, and reviews key their lock on the **PR id**\\\\n(`review.md` §8). One global lock would recreate that class of bug.\\\\n\\\\n**Recursion.**  `autofix.sh` exports `MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1` and refuses\\\\nto start when it is already set.  Without it, `autofix → ci.sh → review.sh →\\\\nautofix` would deadlock on the branch lock and, worse, would let a nested run\\\\ncount fix commits that a parallel run is still making, and slip the cap.  The same variable, with\\\\n`MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1`, is what makes `agent.sh` refuse to run from inside\\\\nthe loop — the local form of `claude.yml:24-30`'s \\\\\\\"skip when sender is a bot\\\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n**Dirty worktree.**  A phase refuses to start when the branch worktree has\\\\nuncommitted changes, because the commit it makes (§6) stages everything.  An\\\\noperator's half-finished edit must not end up inside a bot commit.\\\\n\\\\n## 5. The iteration cap\\\\n\\\\nThe count is derived from the branch's own history, not from a stored field:\\\\ncommits in `merge-base..`*local branch tip* whose subject begins exactly\\\\n`[codex-auto-fix]` or `[codex-review-fix]` (`issues-prs.md` §1).  The **local**\\\\ntip, not the GitHub head: a fix commit that was made but not yet pushed (a\\\\ncrashed run, a failed push) is an ancestor of the local tip only, and the cap\\\\nmust see it or it can never fire.  It counts **fix commits across\\\\nall three kinds**, not per kind — the parent surfaced it to the prompt as\\\\n\\\\\\\"Review-fix iteration N (combined bot-fix cap: M)\\\\\\\" (`auto-fix.yml:391-395`),\\\\ncomputed by the `bot-fix-guard` action (`auto-fix.yml:313-315`).  The default\\\\ncap is 5 (`MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP`).\\\\n\\\\nDeriving it from the commit subjects rather than a counter also removes the\\\\ndrift the old field could develop: the history is the counter.\\\\n\\\\nBefore every phase, if the count is at the cap, the run performs the **cap\\\\nritual** and stops:\\\\n\\\\n1. leave the label in place — the branch history is the counter, so any rerun\\\\n   re-enters this ritual at once and no further automated fix touches the\\\\n   branch;\\\\n2. post an `Auto-fix cap reached — operator review required` PR comment, marked\\\\n   with `<!-- autofix:cap-reached -->` so a repeated run adopts it instead of\\\\n   posting twice;\\\\n3. run `review.sh <id> --force-review` **once**, so the final bot-fix result is\\\\n   reviewed;\\\\n4. exit 0.\\\\n\\\\nStep 3 is not optional.  The review gate skips bot commits (`review.md` §5), so\\\\nwithout a forced review at the cap the last fix commit — the one that would be\\\\nmerged — is the only commit on the branch nobody ever reviewed.\\\\n`pr-review.yml:69-72` names this case explicitly: *we only want to review\\\\nhuman-authored pushes and the final bot-fix result (detected by iteration\\\\ncap)*.  If `review.sh` cannot produce a verdict (a red CI at the cap, say), the\\\\nrun says so loudly and leaves the PR to the operator; it never claims the branch\\\\nwas reviewed.\\\\n\\\\nA PR that reaches the cap is evidence, not just an incident.  Record it in\\\\n`results/telemetry/events.md`; repeated cap hits on similar PRs are the raw\\\\nmaterial for an amendment in `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.\\\\n\\\\n## 6. Commits\\\\n\\\\nEach phase produces **exactly one commit**, whose subject is\\\\n\\\\n    [codex-auto-fix] fix Lean build errors\\\\n    [codex-auto-fix] fix blueprint compilation errors\\\\n    [codex-review-fix] address review findings\\\\n\\\\n`[codex-auto-fix]` for ci and blueprint fixes, `[codex-review-fix]` for review\\\\nfixes.  These strings are not cosmetic: the review gate's regex\\\\n`^\\\\\\\\[(claude|codex)-(auto|review)-fix\\\\\\\\]` (`pr-review.yml:79`) is what stops the\\\\nping-pong, and it matches on the subject.  Change the prefix here without\\\\nchanging the regex there and the loop starts re-reviewing its own fixes, with\\\\nno error anywhere.\\\\n\\\\nThe agent is told not to commit, and the script commits for it.  When an agent\\\\ncommits anyway — they do — `autofix.sh` soft-resets to the pre-run head and\\\\nmakes its own single commit over the resulting tree.  The result is invariant\\\\nregardless of agent behaviour: one commit per iteration, always prefixed, so\\\\nthe counter and the regex both stay honest.\\\\n\\\\nThe commit is made with `git -c user.name=… -c user.email=…` (default\\\\n`codex[bot]`), never by mutating global git config.  Repository hooks are **not**\\\\nbypassed: `.githooks` carries the statement-integrity and blueprint-sync\\\\npre-commit gates (`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`), and a bot commit is exactly\\\\nthe kind of commit they exist to inspect. Prompts and untrusted data\\\\n\\\\nPersona and task prompt come from the committed trusted ref, per pair:\\\\n\\\\n| Mode | Persona | Task |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| ci | `auto-fix-ci-system-prompt.md` | `auto-fix-ci-prompt.md` |\\\\n| blueprint | `auto-fix-blueprint-system-prompt.md` | `auto-fix-blueprint-prompt.md` |\\\\n| review | `auto-fix-review-system-prompt.md` | `auto-fix-review-prompt.md` |\\\\n\\\\nread with `git show \\\\\\\"$MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF:.github/prompts/…\\\\\\\"`, never from the\\\\nbranch being fixed (DESIGN.md invariant 5).  "body": "### Motivation\n- Close #480's concrete Claim 17-2 calculation while accurately distinguishing the proved real-part estimates on the directly indexed subline law from the source complex estimates. The source is `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`, Claims 17-1 through 17-3 and the combined-point lemma.\n\n### Description\n- Prove the concrete X-Z-X scalar estimate from its exact X marginal, expanded line-point consistency, the separate X mixture, and projective Cauchy-Schwarz. Preserve all three scalar theorem signatures and proof bodies.\n- Give each proved scalar estimate a separate auxiliary blueprint entry with its actual distribution, completed evaluations, real-part conclusion, and measurement hypotheses. Keep source-distribution transport, complex comparisons, and concrete paired-line consistency explicitly open.\n- Document the completed point constructor through field-valued commutation, a Z-X-Z sandwich POVM, orthonormalization on the original spaces, and triangle inequalities. Retain the source's binary-refinement route and its ancilla obligation separately.\n- Replace the unused duplicate placement module with an import of the canonical implementation so both paths can coexist. Correct the prefix, Parseval-column, fiber, and Z-only module descriptions.\n\n### Testing\n- Focused Claims, Points, and PlacementSupport build passed; both placement import orders elaborate. C1/C2/C3, the point/subline constructors, and placed measurements use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. Concrete paired-line consistency retains its recorded `sorryAx`.\n- Existing-parser comparison confirms every non-comment token of Claims.lean is unchanged. Source-header checks, blueprint rendering/synchronization, all 1661 declaration links, global completion-marker axiom checks, LaTeX and gap-note checks passed. The gap note compiles to PDF.\n- Normal hooks and checked publication remain enabled. A fresh independent review must exclude all 16 prior corrected-request authors plus repair author `01a082a2-e8d7-7ab3-a512-e4afeec3b820`; the earlier 12-author requests provide no evidence. Exact-head CI and review remain required.\n\n---\nCloses #480\n",
